# University of Jordan
The University of Jordan, established by royal decree in 1962, is the first and largest university in Jordan, with its main campus located in Jubaiha, Amman, spanning 1.20 km². The university began academic operations in 1965 with the Faculty of Arts and has since expanded significantly, adding numerous faculties including Medicine, Engineering, Business, Law, and others. In 2009, it established a branch campus in Aqaba as part of a national strategy to broaden higher education. The university operates with scientific, financial, and administrative autonomy and follows a credit hour system, pioneering such academic frameworks in the Arab world.
Academically, the university offers 78 undergraduate and 143 postgraduate programs across scientific, humanitarian, and medical faculties, with notable accreditation such as ABET for all engineering departments and AACSB for its business school. It houses specialized centers and institutes, including the Jordan University Hospital—the country’s first university teaching hospital—and several research institutes. Its library system (UJL) contains over one million items, including rare manuscripts and international documents. The University of Jordan actively engages in scientific research, publication, and international collaborations, and ranks among the top universities in Jordan and the Arab world according to various global ranking systems. Prominent alumni include political leaders, diplomats, scholars, and professionals who have made significant impacts locally and internationally.
